newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Investor say U.S., Swedish markets boost result.
newsitem.headline: Investor say U.S., Swedish markets boost result.

text.p: Investment company Investor AB, the holding company of Sweden's Wallenberg family, on Tuesday said strong cash flow onto U.S. and Swedish stock markets bolstered its first quarter result.
The company said its total return for the 12 month period ending on March 31 this year was 50 percent compared to 52 percent for the Stockholm Stock Exchange.

The company's net worth was 87.09 billion crowns ($11.2 billion) or 435 crowns per share at the end of the first quarter, an increase of 10 percent since the start of the year. As of April 25 the net worth had fallen to 412 crowns per share.
"Backed by a strong U.S. economy and an easing in the downturn in Europe, the Stockholm Stock Exchange posted good returns during the first two months of the year," Investor said in a statement.
"Another important factor in this positive development was a hefty capital inflow on both the American and Swedish stock markets," Investor said.
The company posted a profit of 114 million crowns for the first quarter of the year after net financial items compared to 12.16 billion for the same 1996 period.
Investor's share slipped after the result, falling 4.5 crowns to 331.5.
Investor posted a one-off gain of 18.80 billion crowns in the first quarter of 1996 from the sale of shares in truck and bus maker Scania, which it spun off and listed on the stock exchange.

The values of the company's main holdings rose by 11 percent in the first quarter of the year adjusted for net changes. This figure compares to a 16 percent rise in the Stockholm Stock Exchange's OMX index.
This was because drug company Astra, Scania and investment company Incentive -- the company's three largest holdings -- performed worse than average on the Stockholm bourse.
"This was counterbalanced to a certain extent by Ericsson, S-E-Banken and SKF performing better than average," Investor said in the statement.
It said it had used part of its cash to buy 3.32 billion crowns worth of shares in S-E-Banken, Scania, Astra and Ericsson in the first quarter and since the end of the quarter
"The background to the significantly increased holding in S-E-Banken is, among other things, the possibility for structural changes that are foreseen in the financial sector," Investor said.
The company said it expects to receive 1.64 billion crowns in dividends this year.

This does not include the value of the dividends in the form of shares of engineering group Granges, which it will receive through its holding in household applicance maker Electrolux, the company said.

Investor said losses in its fully-owned subsidiary Saab AB narrowed to 97 million crowns in the first quarter versus 132 million in Q1 1996. Saab AB makes high-tech products for aerospace and defense.
